## Session A · 2:05–3:15

Counterfactuals and potential outcomes; why every comparison is a claim about a world that did not happen. Causal graphs: confounders, colliders, mediators, back-door reasoning — and why controlling for everything makes things worse. Then the map for the rest of this half: every design we meet is a different way of closing a back door, and you will draw each one before you hear what it is called

## Session B · 3:35–4:30

Every session B opens with a ten-minute team check-in: what you did
since last week, what is stuck, and who is doing what next. Written
down, and handed in with that session's work.

Teams are formed, and then each team writes down its own ground rules — while everybody still gets along, rather than negotiating it in November. Who does what. What happens when somebody misses a deadline. How you settle a disagreement, and when to bring it to me. One page, signed by everyone, handed in before you leave. The weekly check-in starts today

Your team's output is submitted before you leave.
